text:
The search results don't name a specific power station model, so I can't recommend a brand. They do show how to size one, and that's what decides which unit you need.

**Size by watt-hours, not brand.** [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says a portable power station usually beats a UPS for reptile heat. You need sustained watts for hours, not just a clean handoff. Its pure-sine AC outlets can run the heat mat, ceramic heat emitter (CHE) clamp lamp, or thermostat strip you already own. Some units have UPS/EPS pass-through modes, but transfer times vary by brand, so check the maker's page for the model you buy. Its hours are arithmetic, not an overnight test.

**Rough runtimes** (from [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage), also arithmetic, not measured):
- Usable energy is about 85% of the rated capacity, and the station itself draws roughly 5–20 W with AC on.
- A 24 W heat mat plus about 15 W of station draw is about 40 W. A 288 Wh station lasts about 6–8 hours on that, and a 2,073.6 Wh station about two days.
- A 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat at half duty averages about 50 W, plus station draw. That's about a day from 2,073.6 Wh.

**Practical pick:**
- For a heat mat, a station of about 300 Wh covers an overnight outage.
- For a bulb or ceramic emitter, aim for roughly 1,000–2,000 Wh or more.
- Check that the station has a pure-sine AC output and pass-through.
- A Reddit commenter in [r/reptiles](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) says an XL power bank can run a lamp for days. They also say these units are pricier for the wattage but worth it.

**Cheaper options for short outages:**
- Dealectric notes that most pet reptiles handle a short outage in a room in the 60s °F. One vet's guidance for bearded dragons is about a day at 65 °F.
- Cover the enclosure with blankets and keep the room door shut. For small animals, use an insulated container with hand warmers wrapped in cloth.
- [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage) suggests chemical hand warmers, warm water bottles wrapped in towels, or a home generator.
- Don't feed your reptile until temperatures are back to normal, per [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pets-reptiles-during-a-power-outage).

Tell me your heater's wattage and how long an outage you want to cover, and I can work out the capacity you need. If you name a specific model, I can check it against these numbers.
